A material with many small, connected pores can draw in liquid through capillary action, driven by surface tension.
This requires conditions such as wetting of the pore walls and a way for gas in the pores to escape.
Towels absorbing water and blotting paper absorbing ink both involve this effect.

resolvedSectionBreaks.before:
Capillary action can contribute to water transport in plants' narrow tubes and plays a part in plant life.
However, water transport in tall plants cannot be attributed entirely to capillary rise.
Transpiration, the loss of water vapor from plants, and pressure differences also contribute.
